SMTO-CFG-0060 — SMTO can't start because its command output limit is too low

GUID: f3798fd6-4501-468a-bbe7-1a7f4be4fdcc
Slug: config-shell-max-output-chars-must-be-greater
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO stopped while starting because the amount of command output text it keeps is set to zero or less. Your conversations and settings were not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Find where SMTO is started (the terminal command, a startup script or the service settings) and look for a setting named AOR_SHELL_MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS. SMTO reads this output limit from that setting when it starts.
  2. Delete that setting to use the usual 20000 characters, or change it to a positive whole number, such as 20000. With a limit of zero, SMTO could show none of a command's output, so it refuses the value.
  3. Start SMTO again from the same place where you changed the setting. The new limit is used from the next start.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready and commands you run show their output.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO. Don't change the shell access setting or command time limits to clear this error; they control different things.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Settings validation rejected shell_max_output_chars (environment variable AOR_SHELL_MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS) because it is zero or negative.

What this means

  • Effective application settings set shell_max_output_chars at or below zero. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Effective application settings set shell_max_output_chars at or below zero.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the effective shell output character setting and its source override.

How to fix it

  • Unset AOR_SHELL_MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS or set it to a positive integer (default 20000) in the Server's launch environment, then restart; when unset, the already-validated config.yaml runtime.shell_max_output_chars is used (a bad value there fails earlier with a runtime.shell_max_output_chars message). The value becomes the execution engine's max_output_preview_bytes and is separate from shell_command_max_chars.
  • Set shell_max_output_chars to the intended positive character count.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported positive shell output bound is accepted.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
